A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 45-page research work, including Appendices A–J. Text, equations, tables, and figures support a complete comparison; differences are confined to the first-page arXiv stamp and PDF metadata.

before.justification: v3 reports original AI-agent evaluations, human-baseline measurements, fitted time horizons, and robustness experiments in Sections 2–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the same original agent evaluations, human-baseline measurements, time-horizon estimates, and supplementary experimental results.

M1.justification: The time-horizon estimation method and agent scaffold procedures are identical, including the logistic regression formulation and procedures in Appendix C.3–C.4.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HCAST, RE-Bench, SWAA, SWE-bench Verified, internal PR tasks, and filename-randomization scenario. No dataset, task, or evaluation-domain coverage changes.

E2.justification: The model and scaffold rosters, human comparison groups, and comparator membership within corresponding experiments are unchanged, including Tables 4, 6, 7, and 9.

E3.justification: Task selection, human-baselining procedures, scoring thresholds, task weighting, and evaluation settings remain identical in Sections 2–3 and Appendices B, C, and H.

E4.justification: The same failure analyses, messiness studies, alternative curve fits and scoring analyses, inference-cost analysis, and randomized-filename experiment appear in both versions. No supplementary analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Both report approximately eight runs per agent/task pair and 10,000-sample hierarchical bootstrapping. Run-count disclosures, confidence intervals, and statistical reporting practices are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including the 207-day doubling time with a 166–240-day 95% confidence interval and o3's approximately 110-minute horizon in Section 3.2. Appendix result entries also remain identical.

T1.justification: The time-horizon definitions, logistic equations, mathematical reasoning, and comparison with Item Response Theory are unchanged, including Appendix C.4. No formal assumptions or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about the time-horizon metric, SWAA contribution, exponential capability growth, and conditional forecasts of longer-task automation.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning reliability, tool use, human context, task messiness, and future trends are identical. The qualifications about external validity, baselining biases, and extrapolation are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Scaffold and platform descriptions, compute disclosures, baselining details, and code/data access statements remain identical, including Appendices C.3 and I. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 1.1, Appendix A, and all 52 references are unchanged. There is no change in cited research, novelty positioning, or relationships to prior work.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 25 February 2026 to v4 dated 10 July 2026. PDF author metadata adds Chris Painter, who was already visibly credited in v3. The paper's prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page marginal arXiv stamp is repositioned. All figures, tables, captions, and body layouts remain unchanged; rendered pages 2–45 are pixel-identical between versions.

improvement.justification: v4 updates the arXiv stamp and aligns author metadata with an existing visible credit. The scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations, and appendix material remain identical, so these administrative changes produce no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
